# pressR ![pressR hex logo](reference/figures/logo-with-name.png)

**pressR** parses, analyzes, and visualizes pressure distribution data
from capacitive sensor systems. It ships with predefined layouts for
in-shoe pressure measurement, saddle pressure mapping (equine and
bicycle), seating assessment, and barefoot pedography, along with an
interactive Shiny application for data exploration.

## Successor release status

The 0.2.0 development line corrects audited import, unit and
reproducibility problems. The manuscript baseline remains at commit
`5f5b370` (0.1.0). Do not replace a manuscript environment silently:
retain its version and saved cycle references, and review the migration
notes in `NEWS.md`.

To reproduce an analysis that used the frozen manuscript baseline,
install that exact source in a separate R library:

``` r

baseline_lib <- path.expand("~/R/pressR-manuscript-0.1.0")
dir.create(baseline_lib, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
pak::pak("CTTIR/pressR@5f5b370890fafae01b78174a1cec52b4a2039ce3",
         lib = baseline_lib)
# In a fresh R session for that manuscript:
.libPaths(c(baseline_lib, .libPaths()))
```

The successor is experimental software; local software checks do not
establish clinical or study-specific validity.

## Installation

Use R 4.1 or newer. Install the development source and its required
dependencies:

``` r

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("cttir/pressR")
```

HTML reports additionally need `rmarkdown` and Pandoc (included with
RStudio). PDF reports also need a LaTeX installation, such as TinyTeX.
Workbook and archive imports respectively need the optional `readxl` and
`archive` packages.

``` r

install.packages(c("rmarkdown", "tinytex"))  # For HTML and PDF reports
tinytex::install_tinytex()                  # If LaTeX is not already installed
```

## Quick example

``` r

library(pressR)

trial <- pr_example_trial("insole")

pr_plot_heatmap(trial)
pr_plot_force_time(trial, show_cycles = TRUE)

pr_summary(trial)
pr_calc_regional(trial)
pr_run_app(trial)  # Opens the interactive explorer
```

## Features

- **Parsers** for ASCII pressure data exports, generic CSV, force sensor
  data, and region mask files (`.msa`/`.msr`/`.msp`).
- **Predefined layouts** for in-shoe insoles (99-sensor), barefoot
  pressure platforms, generic sensor mats (16x16 / 32x32), horse and
  bicycle saddles, wheelchair / car / office seating, and glove sensors.
- **Per-frame and per-trial analysis**: peak pressure, mean pressure,
  force, contact area, pressure-time integral, center of pressure,
  symmetry index, gait cycle detection, and COP rollover pattern.
- **Application-specific analysis**: saddle bridge and slip detection,
  wheelchair hotspot identification, plantar-pressure regional analysis.
- **Traceable reference observations** with source, study context and
  status. Nyikos (2005) is the source of the six saddle observations;
  unsupported legacy thresholds are withdrawn. Overlays require explicit
  compatible context.
- **Study assets**: lossless workbook cell retention with normalized
  HR/RR series, image metadata registration, bounded archive extraction
  and explicit-key links.
- **Interchange**: version 2 trial bundles preserve exact measurements
  and timing, layout, units, factor levels and metadata with SHA-256
  integrity checks.
- **Visualization**: 2D and 3D heatmaps, dynamics plots, regional bar
  charts, composite report panels, and side-by-side trial comparison.
- **Shiny app**
  ([`pr_run_app()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_run_app.md))
  for interactive import, analysis, and export.

## Real recordings and reproducibility

``` r

trial <- pr_read_auto("recording.asc")
pr_summary_long(trial)  # Values, units, and availability
pr_write_bundle(trial, "recording-bundle")
restored <- pr_read_bundle("recording-bundle")
analysis <- pr_temporal_profile(trial, "corrected")
```

New bundles store authoritative measurements in `measurements.rds` and
provide `pressure.csv` as a nonbinding preview for inspection and
exchange. Reading checks the preview’s checksum and structure; analyses
use the RDS values. Recreate the bundle to change measurements. This
avoids decimal round-trip changes that can invalidate measurement-bound
cycle references. Version 1 bundles remain readable, with their original
decimal precision limits. Only read bundles from trusted sources: they
contain serialized R objects, and checksums detect corruption without
authenticating the sender.

CSV and report exports refuse recorded source paths and symbolic-link
targets. They finish writing before replacing an existing output and
restore it after a reported replacement failure, or report the retained
backup path if restoration fails. These guarantees do not cover process
termination or simultaneous writers.

Pliance detection uses the file header, including temporary upload
paths. CSV round trips recognize exported timestamps and sensor
identifiers. Incomplete or malformed generic inputs are rejected instead
of padded, truncated or zero-filled. Pliance missing-frame handling is
explicit and recorded in metadata.

Numeric text imports accept nonzero magnitudes from `1e-290` through
`1e290` and check for gross conversion errors. These checks add parsing
time: one synthetic 10,000-frame, 256-sensor CSV took 6.59 seconds
versus 0.72 seconds in the preserved baseline on the audit machine, with
identical imported values. This single fixture is not a general
performance guarantee. Version 2 bundles preserve finite binary
measurements beyond that text-import range.

Unknown sensor area or pitch stays unknown. Novel saddle recordings
display in grid units; physical force and contact area remain
unavailable until calibrated. Force-sensor inputs already measured in
newtons are summed directly. Negative sensor offsets are retained and
counted for review.

[`pr_temporal_profile()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_temporal_profile.md)
offers `corrected`, `legacy_method`, and `reference`. Corrected analysis
uses measured timing and deterministic plateau handling. Legacy method
retains the historical 50 Hz assumptions but is not an exact replay
guarantee. Use `pr_lock_cycles(trial, saved_cycles)` for
measurement-bound reference replay. Reports do not silently substitute
historical results or enable reference overlays.

[`pr_inventory()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_inventory.md)
retains every source path and flags identical content.
[`pr_link_assets()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_link_assets.md)
requires explicit acquisition keys and rejects ambiguous joins.
[`pr_read_workbook()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_read_workbook.md)
preserves all sheets, row and column provenance, separate side-by-side
HR series, and invalid observations. Numeric time units require an
explicit choice.
[`pr_read_asset()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_read_asset.md)
registers images; it never converts display colours to temperatures.
Metadata inspection uses ExifTool when installed.

HTML reports require **rmarkdown** and Pandoc; PDF reports additionally
require a working TeX installation. Workbook and archive importers
require **readxl** and **archive**, respectively. The Shiny upload limit
defaults to 128 MiB and can be set through
`options(pressR.max_upload_bytes = ...)` before launching the app.

## Citation

Use `citation("pressR")` for the installed version. Record the package
version and source commit with each analysis. The previously advertised
Zenodo identifier is a draft identifier that does not currently resolve;
it is not presented as a published release DOI.

## Use of LLM tools

Where applicable, LLM tools were used for narrowly defined,
non-authorial tasks: copyediting, prose refinement, Markdown/LaTeX
formatting, boilerplate scaffolding (such as CI configurations and build
scripts), and code refactoring. Tools included [Chat
AI](https://kisski.gwdg.de/leistungen/2-02-llm-service/), the KISSKI
(GWDG) service, and self-hosted **Mistral Small (24B, Apache-2.0)**
served through a local **vLLM architecture** on an Ubuntu Linux
workstation with Intel processors and NVIDIA GPUs. Self-hosted use also
includes models that were further trained (fine-tuned) or weight-edited
in-house for specific tasks. All self-hosted models ran locally, with no
data sent to third parties.

All scientific claims, methodological choices, analyses, interpretations
and conclusions remain the authors’ own. Where applicable, LLM-generated
material must be reviewed and revised before inclusion, and references
must be verified against their DOI, arXiv ID or ISBN.

Local software setup: vLLM with Python/PyTorch, plus R and RStudio.

## Cohort Ingest

Read a whole study into one object: a Pliance/Novel .asc reader that
honours the recorded time column and the device channel map, directory
batch reading, and filename-derived metadata.

- [`pr_read_pliance()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_read_pliance.md)
  : Read a Novel/Pliance ASCII Export

  : Read a Directory of Pressure Exports
- [`pr_meta_from_filename()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_meta_from_filename.md)
  : Split Metadata Fields Out of a File Name

Layouts built from an explicit channel-to-grid index map, for devices
whose channel order is not the grid’s column-major order.

  : Build a Layout From an Explicit Channel Map

  : Novel/Pliance 16x16 Saddle Mat Layout

  : Raw Device Channel Order for a Layout

## Temporal Structure

Spectra and oscillation-based stride detection, for continuously loaded
sensors that never unload between contacts.

- [`pr_calc_spectrum()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_calc_spectrum.md)
  : Power Spectrum of a Frame-Level Signal
- [`pr_calc_dominant_freq()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_calc_dominant_freq.md)
  : Dominant Oscillation Frequency in a Band
- [`pr_calc_stride_cycles()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_calc_stride_cycles.md)
  : Segment a Recording into Stride Cycles
- [`pr_calc_phase_map()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_calc_phase_map.md)
  : Sensor Map Averaged Over the Stride Cycle
- [`pr_cop_shape()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_cop_shape.md)
  : Loop Geometry of a COP Trajectory
- [`pr_temporal_profile()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_temporal_profile.md)
  : Analyze Temporal Structure With an Explicit Reproducibility Profile
- [`pr_lock_cycles()`](https://cttir.github.io/pressR/dev/reference/pr_lock_cycles.md)
  : Bind Historical Cycles to Their Exact Measurements
